title: First substantive phased-array article
why: Turn the saved beam-squint writing brief into an owner-written, reproducible phased-array study and publish it after scientific and editorial review.
done_when: The owner-written article, reproducible code and scientific figures are reviewed, its model assumptions and limitations are explicit, the owner approves publication, and the published article passes site/discovery checks.
success_metrics: A focused question about directional-response loss versus bandwidth, aperture and scan angle.
Reproducible figures and independent checks support the conclusions; no invented measurements or novelty claims.
One owner-approved substantive article is published with correct labels, date, references and discovery outputs.
kill_conditions: Re-scope if the first article expands into an unmanageable multi-effect hardware study.
Do not publish unsupported numerical/physical claims or a manuscript the owner has not approved.

phases.title: Owner manuscript and reproducible evidence
phases.useful_alone: A bounded research question and inspectable manuscript/code/figure package can be reviewed before publication.

items.text: Carry forward the saved beam-squint brief and record the owner’s instruction to close website setup and focus on the first article.

evidence.value: The owner said “Ok” to the proposal, asked to keep it as a reminder, and requested closing the foundation roadmap before the first article. items.text: Owner writes the phased-array manuscript and provides reproducible code/figures; use the saved beam-squint brief as the working direction, with scope refined by the owner.

phases.title: Scientific review and publication
phases.useful_alone: The completed article can be read, checked and followed through the site.

items.text: Review angle/phase conventions, normalization, fixed physical spacing, visible solutions, numerical identities, scientific captions, references and model limits against the actual manuscript/evidence.
